title: Sep 26 Results + Sep 27 Preview: Nice Bounce-Back After Friday's Stumble
summary: Model rebounds with 9-4 showing on Saturday. Mets-Nats rematch tops Sunday's card.

content.value:
## Saturday's Redemption

You know, I've been around this game long enough to know that no model—no matter how sharp—runs the table every night. Friday stung a bit, but Saturday? Saturday was what we call a proper bounce-back. The algorithm went 9-4 with a 69.2% hit rate, and honestly, that's the kind of consistency that wins you money over the long haul.

What I liked most wasn't just the record. It was *how* we got there. The Dodgers pick at 63% confidence? Money. The Rays call at 61%? Cash it. Even some of those coin-flip situations like the Rangers at 51% came through. That's when you know the model's reading the tea leaves correctly.

## The Hits and Misses

Let's talk about what worked. That Dodgers-Giants pick was textbook—we leaned into LA at 63% confidence and they delivered. Same story with the Rays over in Philadelphia. When you're betting 61% and Tampa comes through, that's the model firing on all cylinders.

The misses? Well, the Nationals couldn't hold serve at home against the Mets, the Jays disappointed in Toronto, the Royals let us down in Kansas City, and the Red Sox... look, Boston's been tough to read all month. Four losses on a thirteen-game slate isn't catastrophic, especially when your winners include some solid confidence plays.

## Looking Ahead to Sunday

Here's where it gets interesting. Our top pick for Sunday is the Mets-Nationals rematch in Washington. After the Nats couldn't get it done Saturday, we're flipping the script and backing New York at 52% confidence.

Now, I know what you're thinking—52% isn't exactly a ringing endorsement. But here's the thing: Sean Manaea's been quietly effective down the stretch for the Mets, and DJ Herz, while talented, is still finding his way at the big league level. Sometimes these September series come down to who wants it more, and right now, the Mets have plenty of motivation.

## The Veteran's Take

I've seen enough September baseball to know that momentum matters, but consistency matters more. Saturday's 9-4 record wasn't about getting lucky—it was about the model identifying value in the right spots. When you hit nearly 70% of your picks, you're not guessing.

Sunday's slate will be smaller, as it usually is, but that Mets-Nationals game has all the makings of a sharp play. It's not a hammer-the-window bet, but it's the kind of calculated edge that separates the pros from the weekend warriors.

Stay disciplined, trust the process, and remember: in this business, you don't need to win every day. You just need to win more than you lose.
